claims.text: Low whole grains consumption is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing epidemiological evidence.
Metabolically healthy obesity is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing epidemiological evidence (RR 4.40).
Increased sedentary time is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing epidemiological evidence (HR 1.91).
Low adherence to a healthy dietary pattern is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing evidence (RR 0.80 for highest vs lowest category).
High level of serum uric acid is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing evidence (RR 1.60).
Low level of serum vitamin D is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing evidence (RR 0.62).
Decreased conscientiousness is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing evidence (OR 0.86 per 1 SD increase).
Preterm birth is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing evidence (RR 1.51).
High consumption of sugar-sweetened beverages is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing evidence (RR 1.30).
High level of serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing evidence (HR 1.85 per 1 log unit increase).
Exposure to high level of PM10 air pollution is associated with an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus with convincing evidence (RR 1.34 per 10 ug/m3 increase).
Mendelian randomization studies support a causal association between body mass index (BMI) and risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Mendelian randomization studies do not support a causal relationship between serum C-reactive protein, serum uric acid, or serum vitamin D levels and risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

evidence.description: Meta-analysis of whole grains highest vs. lowest category included 19,107 cases across 9 datasets, yielding RR 0.74 (95% CI: 0.70-0.78, P = 5.45x10^-30) with 0% heterogeneity.
Meta-analysis of metabolically healthy obese vs. metabolically healthy non-obese included 1,285 cases across 10 datasets, yielding RR 4.40 (95% CI: 2.83-6.84, P = 4.97x10^-11).
Meta-analysis of sedentary time highest vs. lowest category included 6,712 cases across 5 datasets, yielding HR 1.91 (95% CI: 1.66-2.19, P = 9.30x10^-20).
Meta-analysis of healthy dietary pattern highest vs. lowest category included 15,574 cases across 18 datasets, yielding RR 0.80 (95% CI: 0.76-0.84, P = 4.86x10^-17).
Meta-analysis of serum uric acid highest vs. lowest category included 5,115 cases across 11 datasets, yielding RR 1.60 (95% CI: 1.44-1.78, P = 4.60x10^-18).
Meta-analysis of serum vitamin D highest vs. lowest category included 5,142 cases across 21 datasets, yielding RR 0.62 (95% CI: 0.54-0.70, P = 1.44x10^-13).
Meta-analysis of conscientiousness per 1 SD increase included 1,845 cases across 5 datasets, yielding OR 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82-0.91, P = 9.94x10^-8).
Meta-analysis of preterm birth vs. normal term included 1,898 cases across 5 datasets, yielding RR 1.51 (95% CI: 1.33-1.72, P = 4.54x10^-10).
Meta-analysis of sugar-sweetened beverages highest vs. lowest category included 30,005 cases across 9 datasets, yielding RR 1.30 (95% CI: 1.21-1.41, P = 2.31x10^-12).
Meta-analysis of serum ALT per 1 log unit increase included 2,009 cases across 14 datasets, yielding HR 1.85 (95% CI: 1.57-2.18, P = 2.85x10^-13).
Meta-analysis of PM10 per 10 ug/m3 increase included 4,974 cases across 4 datasets, yielding RR 1.34 (95% CI: 1.22-1.47, P = 4.26x10^-10).
Multiple Mendelian randomization studies found significant causal odds ratios for BMI on T2DM risk (e.g., OR 1.39, P=0.002; OR 1.27, P=2.0x10^-11).
Mendelian randomization studies for serum CRP (P=0.210-0.230), serum uric acid (P=0.360-0.620), and serum vitamin D (P=0.240-0.940) failed to show statistically significant causal effects.

methodologies.name: Exposure-wide umbrella review and Mendelian randomization evaluation
methodologies.description: Systematic collection and evaluation of existing meta-analyses of observational studies alongside Mendelian randomization studies to evaluate the epidemiological credibility and potential causality of non-genetic risk factors for type 2 diabetes mellitus.

limitations.text: The statistical test for small-study effects should be interpreted with caution in case of large between-study heterogeneity.
Observational component studies did not consistently report sample sizes, making power calculations and excess significance bias estimates potentially conservative.

Genetic instruments of the reviewed Mendelian randomization studies were not directly assessed and power calculations for MR studies could not be performed due to unstated percentage of variance explained.
Observational studies evaluating risk factor associations may suffer from residual confounding or reverse causation.

future_work.text: Conduct randomized clinical trials focusing on strategies to modify harmful daily habits and dietary patterns.
Perform additional well-designed Mendelian randomization studies to clarify causality for observed risk factor associations.
Replicate findings in large-scale environment-wide association studies across diverse ethnic groups.
